content.text: Digital creators in countries where Stripe and PayPal are unavailable face significant barriers when attempting to sell [[LINK:https://coremerch.[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/github-pages-free-digital-product-store-hosting-every-5|GitHub Pages]].io/store/blog/how-how-sell-ebooks-kenya-works-how-deploy-25|ebooks]]. High fees from traditional platforms can erode profits, making it essential to adopt a sovereign infrastructure solution. With NOW[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/payment-options-ethiopian-digital-creators-how-one-creator-5|COREMERCH guide to payment]]s, you can accept Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies at a fraction of the cost, ensuring more revenue from every sale. This guide will walk you through the deployment of a solution that empowers you, the creator, to take control of your sales process.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: How to Start Selling Digital Products with Crypto Payments at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/automated-digital-product-delivery-crypto-explained-digital-creators-6. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.
content.title: How to Start Selling Digital Products with Crypto Payments

content.text: Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail: Bitcoin ebook

Traditional payment platforms often impose high fees and restrictions that can limit your sales potential. For instance, Gumroad charges 10% on every sale, which can quickly add up. In contrast, using NOWPayments only incurs a 0.5% fee, allowing you to retain more of your earnings. This infrastructure not only circumvents the limitations imposed by mainstream payment processors but also provides you with full ownership and control over your digital products and sales data.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before you begin deployment, ensure you have the following: a GitHub account for hosting your store, a NOWPayments account for processing transactions, and a storage solution such as Google Drive for delivering your ebooks. Additionally, prepare your digital products for upload, including ebooks and any associated assets like cover graphics. Familiarize yourself with Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script to handle your backend logic efficiently.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Start by deploying your chosen infrastructure stack, whether it's the Sovereign Starter Stack or the Edge Commerce Stack. Implement NOWPayments to enable Bitcoin transactions, ensuring you configure it to convert pricing to USD at the time of transaction. Next, use Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script to automate the delivery of your ebooks upon successful payment. This setup guarantees that customers receive their products instantly while you maintain complete control over the transaction process.
Retain more revenue with 0.5% fees versus traditional platforms.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once your infrastructure is set up, it's time to go live. Promote your ebook through your chosen channels, directing traffic to your store. Test the purchase process by making a small transaction yourself, ensuring that the payment processing and product delivery work seamlessly. Monitor the transaction in your NOWPayments dashboard to confirm everything functions as expected. This step is crucial for building trust with your customers when you officially launch.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

After successfully processing initial transactions, consider scaling your operations. Utilize the Complete Builder Kit ($197), which includes all six blueprints and seven templates, to enhance your store's functionality. Explore additional payment options and integrate more digital products to expand your offerings. Engage with your customer base through email marketing or social media to drive further sales. The sovereignty of your infrastructure allows you to adapt and grow without being hindered by platform limitations.
How do I sell an ebook online without PayPal or Stripe?

Selling digital products without PayPal or Stripe is not a compromise — it is an upgrade for creators in restricted markets. The conventional platforms that seem like the standard path come with payout delays, geographic restrictions, platform fees of 5 to 10 percent, and the permanent risk of account suspension. A sovereign stack has none of these constraints. Your product page loads on Cloudflare Pages. Your buyer pays in USDT or Bitcoin through a NOWPayments checkout with live price feeds and QR code generation. Your backend verifies the payment on-chain and sends the download link within 30 seconds.
Full ownership of your digital products and customer data.
Related: How Creators Like You Are Building Sovereign Stores

Every digital product type — ebook, course, template, font, preset, beat, plugin, software license — works with the same sovereign commerce infrastructure. You build the product. NOWPayments handles the checkout. Your backend handles the delivery. You keep 99.5% of every sale. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 has COREMERCH deploy the complete stack under your accounts in 48 hours. The Sovereign Blueprint at $47 gives you everything you need to build it yourself. Both paths lead to a store you own completely. See both at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

Build your product before you build your store — the product is the point, not the infrastructure. Once your product is ready and in delivery-ready format, create your NOWPayments account and configure wallet addresses. Choose Stack 01 for self-deployment following the Blueprint, or Stack 02 for COREMERCH deployment. Upload your product file to Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 and note the file path. Configure the product in your backend with the file path, USD price, and delivery email template. Build your product page on the storefront with clear product description, pricing in USD, and the checkout flow. Run a complete mainnet test. Check that the download link works and expires correctly after the configured time period.
